scenes.note: a 3D train interior: its post-processing layer letterboxes the frame over every layer, the clock strip too, so its frames carry the request time only (WE's clock 0.25–0.9 s along, see the 3D notes). The lit train layer flashes on a 2 s alpha loop; the rest is the windows' scrolling buildings (g_Time) and god rays.

fixed 2026-11-06 (fork 7797317, 317bb73): the dog's black box and the upside-down light shafts. Since the scene clock (2026-11-06) the 0.5 s frame is no longer black (0.959 → 0.14: WE's clock was ~1 s ahead, inside the opening fade). The notepad wraps as WE's once ours has Consolas: its 4 pt text in a 195.5 px box fits 21 Consolas characters, 24 of Inconsolata (this system's stand-in, 0.50 em vs 0.55) — the compare now gives ours the Windows fonts. The overall colour is two layers, found by removing layers from a private copy in both WE and ours: the Bliss layer with all its effects matches to 2.2 / 255. (1) The `Clouds` compose layer (id 58: turned 180°, scaled 1.2 × 2.3, `perspective`, procedural_noise with a perspective UV quad) darkens the bottom 30 % of the grass in ours (−14 to −32 / 255) where WE's barely changes anything; without it the grass matches (58,112 vs 59,112). TODO "compose layer turned 180°". (2) The sky's top right: ours' light shafts (`shine`); without them the sky matches (73,95 vs 76,97). WE's shafts are random and showed none in these runs. The clock is the capture's minute.

scenes.note: Was the worst (0.60): WE looked far darker and more saturated. That was the reference, not us. At Ultra WE presents an HDR scene through an FP16 (scRGB) swap chain holding lin () of the picture; Windows sRGB-encodes it for an SDR display, DXVK under Proton showed it raw. The frames are re-encoded now (we-proton.md "The FP16 swap chain"), and ours matches. The rest is camera shake (random).
